title: Mount Sinai Candidates Explorer
subtitle: Compare traditions and proposals while the biblical mountain remains unlocated
summary: A MapLibre comparison scene separates the unlocated biblical Sinai/Horeb from mapped traditional, candidate, and broad regional proposal records.
disclaimer: Mount Sinai/Horeb is not assigned a definitive modern coordinate. Selecting an option moves the camera to an existing traditional site, candidate site, or broad regional orientation record; it does not raise that option to established status. Real relief appears only when a separately verified DEM is configured.

evidenceLegend.label: Real terrain if DEM configured
evidenceLegend.description: Physical elevation can be real while the biblical identification remains uncertain.

evidenceLegend.label: Traditional identification
evidenceLegend.description: A later historical identification is shown as tradition, not archaeological proof of the Exodus mountain.

evidenceLegend.label: Proposal geography
evidenceLegend.description: A candidate or regional orientation used to examine travel geography and scholarly proposals.

evidenceLegend.label: Unknown / disputed
evidenceLegend.description: The biblical mountain itself remains without a definitive modern coordinate.

periods.label: Candidate comparison
periods.note: This mode compares geographic proposals; it does not assign a precise date to the Exodus or Sinai covenant narrative.

entryCamera.note: Broad overview camera only, centered between existing candidate/orientation records; it is not a biblical-place coordinate.

comparison.label: Sinai / Horeb alternatives
comparison.intro: The biblical place remains unlocated. Camera movement is a comparison tool, not a confidence upgrade.

options.label: Jebel Musa tradition
options.summary: Jebel Musa in southern Sinai is mapped because of its long Christian traditional identification with Mount Sinai.
options.rationale: The v1 record treats Jebel Musa as a significant traditional identification, especially from late antiquity onward.
options.objections: Tradition is not equivalent to archaeological proof that this is the mountain of Exodus, and the biblical Mount Sinai record remains unlocated.

camera.note: Camera uses the existing Jebel Musa traditional-site coordinate from the atlas.

options.label: Har Karkom proposal
options.summary: Har Karkom is included as a specific southern-Negev proposal for Sinai/Horeb rather than as an established identification.
options.rationale: The v1 record preserves the proposal so users can inspect a concrete alternative and its geography.
options.objections: The proposal is controversial, including chronology and interpretation questions, and is not treated as a consensus identification.

camera.note: Camera uses the existing Har Karkom candidate-site coordinate from the atlas.

options.label: Northwestern Arabia family
options.summary: Some proposals place Sinai east of the Gulf of Aqaba in northwestern Arabia; this option intentionally uses only the atlas broad Midian orientation rather than inventing a candidate mountain pin.
options.rationale: The v1 Sinai interpretation record preserves northwestern-Arabia proposals as disputed alternatives, and the Midian record supplies a broad approximate-area orientation.
options.objections: This option does not identify a specific mountain. The extent of Midian varied, and a broad regional anchor cannot establish the location of biblical Sinai.

camera.note: Camera reuses the existing Midian approximate-area orientation; it is deliberately not a candidate-site coordinate.

hotspots.label: Jebel Musa
hotspots.summary: Traditional Mount Sinai identification in southern Sinai, shown as tradition only.

whyShown.evidence: The existing place record maps Jebel Musa as a traditional-site coordinate.
whyShown.inference: Its surrounding terrain can be explored as the landscape of a tradition, not as recovered Exodus geography.
whyShown.alternatives: Har Karkom and northwestern-Arabia proposal families remain separate; biblical Mount Sinai itself stays unlocated.

hotspots.label: Har Karkom
hotspots.summary: A mapped candidate proposal in the southern Negev whose identification with Sinai/Horeb is disputed.

whyShown.evidence: The v1 atlas includes Har Karkom as a candidate-site record.
whyShown.inference: The map lets users examine its geography without adopting the proposal.
whyShown.alternatives: Other northern/central, southern-Sinai, and east-of-Aqaba proposals exist; no consensus identification is asserted.

hotspots.label: Midian: broad orientation only
hotspots.summary: This broad regional anchor is used to discuss northwestern-Arabia proposal families without inventing a mountain coordinate.

whyShown.evidence: The atlas associates Midian broadly with northwestern Arabia and adjacent areas, with an approximate-area coordinate.
whyShown.inference: That broad geography is relevant to some Sinai arguments but does not identify Horeb/Sinai.
whyShown.alternatives: The proposal family must not be reduced to one modern mountain unless a specific candidate is separately sourced and labeled.
